abstract: Despite the rapid progress of on-chip photonic computing, optical neural networks (ONNs) remain constrained by limited kernel expressivity, weak nonlinearities, and substantial hardware overhead. To address these limitations, we propose a compact microring resonator (MRR)-based photonic convolutional neural network (PCNN) for modulation format classification from constellation diagrams. This architecture is based on cascaded dual-microring units and add–drop MRRs; the former achieves dual-port mixing in the optical linear layer through a phase compensation mechanism while the latter utilizes differential pass-through and up/down-link readout to implement signed convolution kernel coefficients. On constellation diagrams derived from the RML2016.10a dataset, the proposed PCNN achieves accuracies of 82.58%, 87.85%, and 91.94% at input resolutions of 16×16, 32×32, and 48×48, respectively, with only 0.25 million trainable parameters and 0.001 GFLOPs. We further provide an explicit physics-to-network parameter mapping and a first-order implementation-budget analysis, indicating a compact and programmable photonic route to modulation format recognition under tight computational and hardware budgets.
title: Lightweight programmable microring resonator photonic convolutional neural network for modulation format classification
